description_full: Schaeffler AG, together with its subsidiaries, develops, manufactures, and sells components and systems for industrial applications in Europe, the Americas, China, and the Asia Pacific. It operates through E-Mobility, Powertrain and Chassis, Vehicle Lifetime Solutions, Bearings & Industrial Solutions divisions. The E-Mobility division offers mechanical, mechatronic, and electronic components and systems for powertrain electrification used in passenger cars and commercial vehicles. It includes electric drives, controls, and mechatronics and modules, as well as battery components, decoupling units, and wet clutches. The Powertrain & Chassis division develops, manufactures, and distributes components and system solutions for electrified powertrains and internal combustion engine, as well as chassis and steering technologies. This segment also provides engine and transmission systems, powertrain solutions, and chassis systems; torque converters, hybrid dampers, clutches, variable valve train systems, valve-lash adjustment elements, balancer shafts, camshaft phasing systems, timing drives, and front end auxiliary drives. The Vehicle Lifetime Solutions division offers components and repair solutions for passenger cars, light and heavy commercial vehicles, tractors, and two-wheelers. The Bearings & Industrial Solutions division develops, manufactures, and distributes rotary and linear bearing solutions, drive components and systems for industrial automation sectors, and service solutions. It has a strategic technology partnership with Hexagon Robotics for the development and supply of high-precision strain wave and planetary gear actuators. The company was formerly known as INA Beteiligungsgesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung and changed its name to Schaeffler AG in October 2014. Schaeffler AG was founded in 1946 and is headquartered in Herzogenaurach, Germany. Schaeffler AG operates as a subsidiary of IHO Verwaltungs GmbH.

financial_summary: SCHAEFFLER AG is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $6.0B market cap on $26.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +17% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 8% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 21% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The business throws off $425M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
Accruals are elevated at -8.5% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.7× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 0.8× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.6% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 79% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
